items.m03s3q4: Overall, attendance at the Science Museum rose strongly throughout the decade, whereas both the Art Gallery and the History Museum saw a gradual decline. Although the Art Gallery was the most visited at the start, the Science Museum had overtaken it by the middle of the period, and the History Museum remained the least popular throughout.
items.m03s3q5: Overall, the mix of electricity sources changed considerably over the two decades. Coal lost more than half of its share and was overtaken by natural gas, which became the leading source, while wind and solar grew from a minor contributor to one of the largest. Nuclear and hydro, by contrast, remained almost unchanged.
items.m03ckq8: Overall, the youngest group spent the most time on social media and gaming, and both of these activities fell sharply with age. Streaming video, on the other hand, was remarkably similar across all four groups, which made it the leading activity for people aged 30 and over.
items.m04s3q5: The Science Museum grew steadily from just over 400 thousand visitors in 2010 to nearly 760 thousand in 2020, almost doubling over the decade.
items.m04s3q6: Teenagers spent 21 hours a week on social media, more than three times as long as people aged over 50, who spent only 6 hours.
items.m04ckq8: The share of electricity generated from coal fell from 48% in 2000 to just 18% in 2020, a drop of 30 percentage points.
items.m06s3q7: The Science Museum received around 420 thousand visitors in 2010, considerably fewer than the Art Gallery's 610 thousand. Its numbers then climbed steadily, overtaking the Art Gallery in 2014 with 570 thousand against 560 thousand, and reached approximately 760 thousand by 2020, almost double the initial figure. By then it attracted nearly three times as many visitors as the History Museum.
items.m07s3q7: German teachers were the best paid at both career stages, starting on 62000 dollars and earning 81000 after 15 years. At the other extreme, Thai teachers earned 9000 and 17000 dollars respectively, so a new German teacher was paid almost seven times as much as a Thai colleague. Japan, Korea and the USA fell in between, with starting salaries of 31000, 33000 and 44000 dollars.
items.m08s3q7: Overall, the recycling of glass bottles is a cyclical, man-made process with eight main stages. It begins with the collection of used bottles at a bottle bank and ends when the newly made bottles are filled and delivered to shops, after which the cycle repeats.
items.m09s3q7: Overall, the centre of Riverside was transformed from an industrial and commercial district into a largely residential and leisure area. The factory gave way to apartment blocks, and traffic was moved out of the centre by pedestrianising the main road and building a ring road, while the river, the park and the bus station remained unchanged.
items.m10s3q7: Finland consumed by far the most coffee, at 21 cups per person per week, half as much again as Italy, which came second with 14 cups. Brazil followed closely with 12 cups, whereas Japan and Thailand drank considerably less, at 8 and 5 cups respectively. Thai consumption was therefore less than a quarter of the Finnish figure.

plan.big: Science Museum increased strongly, Art Gallery and History Museum both fell, Science overtook Art around 2014

slots.what: how many visitors, in thousands, went to three museums in a European city
slots.groupB: the Art Gallery and the History Museum
slots.feature: the Science Museum overtook the Art Gallery in around 2014 and the History Museum was the least popular in every year

p-line-museums.text:
The line graph shows how many visitors, in thousands, went to three museums in a European city from 2010 to 2020.

Overall, the number of visitors to the Science Museum increased strongly over the whole period, while both the Art Gallery and the History Museum lost visitors. The Science Museum overtook the Art Gallery in around 2014, and the History Museum was the least popular museum in every year.

In 2010 the Science Museum had 420 thousand visitors, which was less than the Art Gallery. However, it rose steadily to 570 thousand in 2014 and 710 thousand in 2018, and it reached a peak of 760 thousand in 2020. This was nearly twice the figure for 2010.

In contrast, the Art Gallery started as the most visited museum, with 610 thousand visitors in 2010, but its numbers fell to 560 thousand in 2014 and 520 thousand in 2020. The History Museum also declined, from 380 thousand in 2010 to only 260 thousand in 2020, although there were a small increase to 300 thousand in 2018.

The Science Museum rose from 420 thousand visitors in 2010 to 570 thousand in 2014 and 710 thousand in 2018, and it reached a peak of 760 thousand in 2020, nearly twice the figure for 2010.

In contrast, the Art Gallery fell from 610 thousand in 2010 to 520 thousand in 2020, and the History Museum, which was the least popular in every year, declined from 380 thousand to 260 thousand.

plan.big: youngest spent most on social media and gaming, both fell sharply with age; streaming similar for all and the main activity over 30

slots.what: the weekly hours that four different age groups in one country spent on social media, streaming video and gaming in 2023
slots.contrast: social media and gaming fell sharply with age, but streaming video was similar in all four groups
slots.figA: 21 hours for teenagers, compared with only 6 hours for people over 50
slots.figB: between 12 and 15 hours in every group
slots.exception: streaming video, which was the main activity for people aged 30 and over

p-bar-screentime.text:
The bar chart compares the weekly hours that four different age groups in one country spent on social media, streaming video and gaming in 2023.

Overall, the youngest group spent the most time on social media and gaming, and both of these activities fell sharply with age. Streaming video, however, was similar in all four groups and was the main activity for people aged 30 and over.

Teenagers aged 13–17 spent 21 hours a week on social media, compared with 18 hours for the 18–29 group. The two older groups used social media much less, at 11 hours for 30–49-year-olds and only 6 hours for people over 50. Gaming followed the same pattern, falling from 12 hours for teenagers to just 1 hour for the over-50s.

In contrast, streaming video was between 12 and 15 hours in all of four groups. The 18–29 group watched the most, at 15 hours, and the 30–49 group the least, at 12 hours. For people aged 50 and over, streaming, at 13 hours, took more time than social media and gaming put together.

plan.big: man-made cyclical process, eight stages, from bottle bank to shops; two phases: preparing waste glass and producing new bottles
plan.gb: stages 5 to 8: making the new bottles

slots.product: how used glass bottles are recycled and made into new bottles
slots.start: used bottles in a bottle bank
slots.st1: people put their empty bottles into a bottle bank and they are transported by lorry to a recycling plant
slots.st2: they are washed with high-pressure water
slots.st3: they are sorted by colour into clear, green and brown glass and then crushed into small pieces, which are called cullet
slots.st4: is melted in a furnace at 600 to 800 °C with new raw materials
slots.st5: the molten glass is moulded into new bottles
slots.st6: the bottles are filled and delivered to shops, and the cycle starts again

p-proc-glass.text:
The diagram shows the process by which used glass bottles are recycled and made into new bottles.

Overall, this is a man-made and cyclical process with eight stages. It begins when used bottles are collected at a bottle bank and ends when new bottles are delivered to shops, and the stages can be divided into two phases: preparing the waste glass and producing the new bottles.

At the first stage, people put their empty bottles into a bottle bank. The bottles are then transported by lorry to a recycling plant, where they are washed with high-pressure water. Next, they are sorted by colour into clear, green and brown glass, and after that the glass is crushed into small pieces, which is called cullet.

In the second phase, the cullet is melted in a furnace at a temperature of 600 to 800 °C, and new raw materials are added. The molten glass is then moulded into new bottles. Finally, the bottles are filled and delivered to shops, and once they have been used, they go back to the bottle bank and the cycle starts again.

slots.place: the centre of a small town in the north-east of Thailand
slots.change: became much more modern and built-up
slots.where1: south-west, south of the main road
slots.where2: south-east, on most of the rice fields
slots.extended: the main road, which crosses the whole town, was widened to four lanes
slots.converted: the open field next to the market

p-map-thai-town.text:
The two maps show how the centre of a small town in the north-east of Thailand changed between 2005 and 2025.

Overall, the town centre became much more modern and built-up over the twenty years. Most of the old buildings were replaced by new ones on the same sites, and a hospital was built on the rice fields, while the river and the temple stayed the same.

North of the main road, the wet market in the west was rebuilt as a covered market, and the open field next to it became a car park. The temple in the north-east corner did not change. The main road, which crosses the whole town from the river to the east, was widened to four lanes.

South of the road, the wooden houses in the south-west were knocked down and replaced by townhouses. In the south-east, a hospital was constructed on the most of the rice fields, so only a small area of rice fields remained in the corner. Finally, the ferry crossing on the river was replaced by a bridge in the same place.

plan.big: smartphones rose sharply and basic phones fell at almost the same rate; lines crossed between 2013 and 2016

slots.what: what proportion of teenagers in one country had a smartphone and what proportion had a basic mobile phone
slots.moveB: fell at almost the same rate
slots.feature: the two lines crossed between 2013 and 2016, and by 2025 almost every teenager owned a smartphone

p-line-phones.text:
The line graph shows what proportion of teenagers in one country had a smartphone and what proportion had a basic mobile phone from 2010 to 2025.

Overall, smartphone ownership rose sharply over the period, while basic phone ownership fell at almost the same rate, so the two lines were nearly mirror images. They crossed between 2013 and 2016, and by 2025 almost every teenager owned a smartphone and very few owned a basic phone.

In 2010, only 10% of teenagers had a smartphone. This figure rose quickly to 30% in 2013 and 60% in 2016, when smartphones became more common than basic phones for the first time. After that the growth was slowed down, but ownership still reached 80% in 2019, 90% in 2022 and 95% in 2025.

Basic phones showed the opposite trend. In 2010, 80% of teenagers owned one, but this fell to 65% in 2013 and 40% in 2016. The decline continued to 20% in 2019 and 10% in 2022, and by 2025 only 5% of teenagers still had a basic phone, which was 75 percentage points lower than in 2010.

mocks.mock1:
The line graph shows the proportion of households that had internet access in four countries, Sweden, Japan, Thailand and Kenya, from 2005 to 2025.

Overall, internet access increased in all four countries over the period. Sweden and Japan had high figures from the start and ended close together near full coverage, whereas Thailand showed the biggest rise and Kenya stayed the lowest in every year despite strong growth.

Sweden was the leader throughout, rising from 70% of households in 2005 to 92% in 2015 and 97% in 2025. Japan began lower, at 60%, but it grew quickly to 78% in 2010 and 88% in 2015, and by 2025 it was at 95%, only slightly below Sweden.

In contrast, just 12% of households in Thailand had internet access in 2005. This figure rose steeply to 52% in 2015 and 88% in 2025, so Thailand almost caught up with Japan. Kenya started at only 2% and, although it reached 35% in 2020 and 52% in 2025, it remained far behind the other three countries.
mocks.mock2:
The table shows how much rice, in million tonnes, was produced by China, India, Vietnam and Thailand in 2000, 2010 and 2020.

Overall, China produced the most rice in every year, but India had the largest increase over the two decades. Vietnam and Thailand produced far less than the two larger countries, and Thailand was the only one whose production fell between 2010 and 2020.

China's production rose from 188 million tonnes in 2000 to 197 million in 2010 and then to 212 million in 2020. India started much lower, at 127 million tonnes, but it increased to 144 million in 2010 and 178 million in 2020, which was a rise of over 50 million tonnes in total.

The two smaller producers had very different figures. Vietnam's output grew slowly, from 32 million tonnes in 2000 to 40 million in 2010 and 43 million in 2020. Thailand, on the other hand, rose from 26 million to 36 million tonnes in 2010 but then dropped back to 30 million in 2020, so it finished as the smallest producer.
mocks.mock3:
The two maps show a secondary school campus as it is at present and how it will look after the planned changes.

Overall, the plan adds new buildings and green space, mainly by reducing the size of the sports field. The library and the car park will both move to new sites, while the main building and the road will stay the same.

At present, the main building is in the north-west corner next to the road, and the car park is in the north-east. The library and the canteen are side by side in the centre of the campus, with an area of open ground to the east of them, and the sports field runs along the whole of the south side.

In the plan, the car park will become a garden, and a new car park will be built on the open ground in the centre-east. The canteen will be extended west into the space where the library is now, and a new library will be built in the south-west, on part of the sports field, which will be reduced to about half its current size.
